text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, usually using methods like GET or POST. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can use many APIs, you need authentication, often through an API key, to prove who you are. APIs also have rate limits, which control how many requests you can make in a certain time. Finally, good error handling is essential, because requests can fail for many reasons, and your program should respond gracefully instead of crashing.
